references.text: The crowd demanded that Barabbas, who had been imprisoned for rebellion and murder, be released ([ref:Luk 23:18-19|Luke 23:18-19]). Verse 25 confirms that Pilatus granted this request.
Pilatus originally intended to have Jesus flogged and then release him ([ref:Luk 23:16-17|Luke 23:16-17]), but the crowd's demand led him instead to hand Jesus over to their will.
The parallel account in [ref:Matt 27:26|Matthew 27:26] describes the same thing: Pilatus released Barabbas and handed Jesus over to be crucified.
Mark's parallel account in [ref:Mark 15:15|Mark 15:15] tells that Pilatus, to satisfy the crowd, released Barabbas and handed Jesus over to be crucified.
John's parallel account in [ref:Joh 19:16|John 19:16] says that Pilatus handed Jesus over to them so that he might be crucified.
In [ref:Joh 18:40|John 18:40], the crowd cries out that they want Barabbas released, not Jesus – Barabbas is described there as a robber.
Peter refers to this event in his speech in [ref:Apg 3:13-14|Acts 3:13-14], where he accuses the people of having denied the Holy and Righteous One and asked for a murderer to be set free.

In the believers' prayer in [ref:Apg 4:27-28|Acts 4:27-28], it is mentioned that Herod and Pontius Pilatus, together with the Gentiles and the people of Israel, gathered against Jesus – but that this happened according to God's counsel and will.
The prophecy in [ref:Jes 53:6|Isaiah 53:6] that the Lord laid on him the guilt of us all finds its fulfillment as Jesus is handed over for crucifixion while the guilty Barabbas goes free.
In [ref:Jes 53:12|Isaiah 53:12] it is prophesied that the Lord's servant was counted among transgressors – Jesus was handed over in place of criminals, while the murderer Barabbas was set free.

Paul mentions in [ref:Apg 13:28|Acts 13:28] that the people of Jerusalem, although they found no ground for death in Jesus, asked Pilatus to have him killed – which corresponds to Pilatus handing Jesus over to their will.
